XV.|TO THE ROMANES.|419}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, scrolling foliage with grotesque heads.png|imgsize=140px|fl={{verse|chapter=15|verse=1}}}}ND vve that are the stronger, must susteine the infirmities of the vveake, & not please our selues. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=2}}† Let euery one of you please his neighbour vnto good, to edification. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=3}}† For, Christ did not please him self, but as it is vvritten, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Psa. 68, 10.''}}* ''The reproches of them that reproched thee, fel vpon me''. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=4}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpō the 2. Sunday in Aduent.}}For {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ He meaneth al that is vvritten in the old Testamēt: much more al things written in the new Testamēt, are for our learning and comfort.}}∷ vvhat things soeuer haue been vvritten, to our learning they are vvritten: that by the patience and consolation of the Scriptures, vve may haue hope. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=5}}† And the God of patience and of comfort giue you to be of one minde one tovvard an other according to {{sc|Iesvs}} Christ: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=6}}† that of {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Vnitie in religion commended.}}∷ one minde, vvith one mouth you may glorifie God and the Father of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}} Christ. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=7}}† For the vvhich cause receiue one an other: as Christ also hath receiued you vnto the honour of God. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=8}}† For I say Christ {{sc|Iesvs}} to haue been {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Christ did execute his office and ministerie onely towards the people of Circumcision, that is, the Iewes.}}∷ minister of the circumcision for the veritie of God, to confirme the promisses of the fathers. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=9}}† But the Gentils to honour God for his mercie, as it is vvritten: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Psa. 17, 50.''}}* ''Therfore vvil I confesse to thee in the Gentils ô Lord, and vvil sing to thy name''. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=10}}† And againe he saith, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 32, 43.''}}* ''Reioyce ye Gentils vvith his people''. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=11}}† And againe, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Psa. 116, 1.''}}* ''Praise al ye Gentils our Lord: and magnifie him al ye peoples''. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=12}}† And againe Esaie saith, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 11, 10.''}}* ''There shal be the roote of Iesse: and he that shal rise vp to rule the Gentils, in him the Gentils shal hope''. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=13}}† And the God of hope replenish you vvith al ioy and peace in beleeuing: that you may abound in hope, and in the vertue of the holy Ghost.⊣

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=14}}† And I my self also, my brethren, am assured of you, that you also are ful of loue, replenished vvith al knowledge, so that you are able to admonish one an other. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=15}}† But I haue vvritten to you (brethren) more boldly in part, as it were putting you in remembrance: for the grace vvhich is giuen me of God, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=16}}† to be the minister of Christ {{sc|Iesvs}} in the Gentils: sanctifying the Gospel of God, that the oblation of the Gentils may be made acceptable and sanctified in the holy<noinclude>{{rh||Ggg ij|Ghost.}}</noinclude>
